claim: DLBCL is the predominant type of malignant B-cell lymphoma.
source: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the predominant type of malignant B-cell lymphoma.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a background statement about DLBCL.

claim: DLBCL accounts for around 30% of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
source: DLBCL is the most prevalent type among them, accounting for around 30% of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
evidence: This is a cited statistic in the introduction providing epidemiological context.

claim: DLBCL was initially classified by the Hans algorithm into two subtypes: germinal center B-cell-like (GCB) and non-GCB.
source: DLBCL was initially classified by the Hans algorithm into two subtypes: germinal center B-cell-like (GCB) and non-GCB (Hans et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hans et al., 2004.

claim: Three distinct gene-based subtypes of DLBCL have been identified: GCB, activated B-cell-like (ABC), and the unclassified category.
source: Further differentiation has since identified three distinct gene-based subtypes: GCB, activated B-cell-like (ABC), and the unclassified category (Sehn and Salles, 2021).
evidence: This classification is supported by citation to Sehn and Salles, 2021.

claim: About 60% of DLBCL patients achieve long-term remission after undergoing R-CHOP chemotherapy.
source: After undergoing R-CHOP chemotherapy, about 60% of patients achieve long-term remission; however, approximately 30% of patients experience relapse, resulting in poor prognosis and a considerable number of deaths from refractory lymphoma (Autio et al., 2021).
evidence: This treatment outcome statistic is supported by citation to Autio et al., 2021.

claim: Approximately 30% of DLBCL patients experience relapse after R-CHOP chemotherapy.
source: After undergoing R-CHOP chemotherapy, about 60% of patients achieve long-term remission; however, approximately 30% of patients experience relapse, resulting in poor prognosis and a considerable number of deaths from refractory lymphoma (Autio et al., 2021).
evidence: This relapse rate is supported by citation to Autio et al., 2021.

claim: The tumor microenvironment (TME) is a complex and dynamic system that consists of the extracellular matrix and a variety of cellular components.
source: The tumor microenvironment (TME) is a complex and dynamic system that consists of the extracellular matrix and a variety of cellular components.
evidence: This is a general statement about TME composition based on established knowledge.

claim: Multiple subgroups of immune cells exist within the microenvironment of DLBCL, including T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes/macrophages, and dendritic cells.
source: Recent studies have unveiled multiple subgroups of immune cells within the microenvironment of DLBCL, including T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, as well as the distribution of stromal cell components like fibroblasts and endothelial cells (Steen et al., 2021; Ciavarella et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement about immune cell composition is supported by citations to Steen et al., 2021 and Ciavarella et al., 2018.

claim: Stromal cell components like fibroblasts and endothelial cells are distributed in the DLBCL microenvironment.
source: Recent studies have unveiled multiple subgroups of immune cells within the microenvironment of DLBCL, including T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, as well as the distribution of stromal cell components like fibroblasts and endothelial cells (Steen et al., 2021; Ciavarella et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement about stromal components is supported by citations to Steen et al., 2021 and Ciavarella et al., 2018.

claim: The interaction between tumors and the microenvironment is a vital factor that impacts the development and prognosis of B-cell lymphoma.
source: The interaction between tumors and the microenvironment is a vital factor that impacts the development and prognosis of B-cell lymphoma (Ennishi et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Ennishi et al., 2020.

claim: A higher quantity of extracellular matrix in DLBCL is associated with a more favorable prognosis.
source: Previous research on stroma in DLBCL has predominantly indicated that a higher quantity of extracellular matrix is associated with a more favorable prognosis, while increased vascular density is associated with poorer prognosis (Miyawaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citation to Miyawaki et al., 2022.

claim: Increased vascular density in DLBCL is associated with poorer prognosis.
source: Previous research on stroma in DLBCL has predominantly indicated that a higher quantity of extracellular matrix is associated with a more favorable prognosis, while increased vascular density is associated with poorer prognosis (Miyawaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citation to Miyawaki et al., 2022.

claim: Higher stromal scores have been associated with an improved prognosis in DLBCL patients.
source: Furthermore, higher stromal scores have been associated with an improved prognosis in DLBCL patients (Schmitz et al., 2018).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citation to Schmitz et al., 2018.

claim: A fibrotic tumor microenvironment has been correlated with a better prognosis after DLBCL chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
source: Additionally, a fibrotic tumor microenvironment has been correlated with a better prognosis after DLBCL chemotherapy and immunotherapy (Lou et al., 2022).
evidence: This prognostic correlation is supported by citation to Lou et al., 2022.

claim: Tumor purity quantifies the relative ratio of tumor cells to the surrounding stromal components in solid tumors.
source: Tumor purity quantifies the relative ratio of tumor cells to the surrounding stromal components in solid tumors, elucidating the dynamics between tumor cells and their microenvironment (Gong et al., 2020).
evidence: This definition is supported by citation to Gong et al., 2020.

claim: A higher tumor purity indicates a lower abundance of stromal components in TME.
source: It can partly reflect the characteristics of TME, namely, a higher tumor purity indicates a lower abundance of stromal components in TME.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the definition of tumor purity.

claim: Tumor purity is associated with patients' prognosis, and the strength of this association varies across different tumor types.
source: Tumor purity is associated with patients' prognosis, and the strength of this association varies across different tumor types (Lou et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lou et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: 642 genes were identified as tumor purity-related genes (TPGs) in DLBCL, with 31 genes positively correlated and 611 genes negatively correlated with tumor purity.
source: According to the thresholds mentioned above, 642 genes were identified as TPGs, among which 31 genes were positively correlated with tumor purity, while 611 genes were negatively correlated with it (Figure 2B).
evidence: This finding is based on correlation analysis of gene expression data from GSE53786 dataset and is shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Tumor purity in DLBCL ranged from 17.2 to 67.4% in the GSE53786 dataset.
source: Based on GSE53786 dataset, we first assessed the tumor purity of DLBCL, which ranged from 17.2 to 67.4% (Figure 2A).
evidence: This range is calculated from the GSE53786 dataset using ESTIMATE algorithm and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Patients with high tumor purity had lower OS rates than those with low tumor purity in DLBCL.
source: In addition, tumor purity did have influence on the prognosis of DLBCL patients, which showed that patients with high tumor purity had lower OS rates than those with low tumor purity (Figure 2C, p=0.025).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on GSE53786 dataset with statistical significance (p=0.025) and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TPGs were mainly associated with extracellular matrix organization and immune response.
source: It turned out that the TPGs were mainly associated with extracellular matrix organization and immune response (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This functional association is determined by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Nine genes (LUM, VCAN, YAP1, COL5A2, SDC2, TWIST1, CD3G, C1QB, and C3) were identified as intersection genes between PPI hub genes and prognostic TPGs.
source: Through conducting intersection analysis, we found nine genes (LUM, VCAN, YAP1, COL5A2, SDC2, TWIST1, CD3G, C1QB, and C3) were intersection genes (Figure 3D), indicating that they had an active effect in modulating the tumor purity, as well as influencing the prognosis of DLBCL patients.
evidence: This finding is based on intersection analysis of PPI hub genes and prognostic genes, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: VCAN and CD3G were correlated with good prognosis in DLBCL.
source: It showed that VCAN and CD3G were correlated with good prognosis and C1QB was correlated with poor prognosis.
evidence: This prognostic association is determined from the Cox regression model construction shown in Figure 4A.

claim: C1QB was correlated with poor prognosis in DLBCL.
source: It showed that VCAN and CD3G were correlated with good prognosis and C1QB was correlated with poor prognosis.
evidence: This prognostic association is determined from the Cox regression model construction shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The high-risk group has worse prognosis than the low-risk group based on the riskScore model.
source: As expected, the high-risk group has worse prognosis than the low-risk group (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by survival analysis in the GSE53786 dataset shown in Figure 4C.

claim: High-risk group had lower OS rate than low-risk group in GSE53786 dataset (p<0.001).
source: High-risk group had lower OS rate than low-risk group (Figure 4E, p<0.001)
evidence: This survival difference is statistically significant (p<0.001) as shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The AUC for 1 year, 3 year, and 5 year ROC were 0.73, 0.77, and 0.77, respectively, in GSE53786 dataset.
source: the areas under curve (AUC) for 1 year, 3 year, and 5 year ROC were 0.73, 0.77, and 0.77, respectively (Figure 4F).
evidence: These AUC values are calculated from ROC analysis of the prognostic model in GSE53786 dataset, shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Tumor purity was positively correlated with riskScore in GSE53786 dataset.
source: Just similar to tumor purity, the high riskScore indicated bad outcome, which was consistent with the positive correlation between tumor purity and riskScore (Figure 4G).
evidence: This correlation is shown in Figure 4G based on analysis of GSE53786 dataset.

claim: High-risk group had more ABC type DLBCL, while low-risk group had more GCB type DLBCL.
source: The results showed that high-risk group had more ABC type DLBCL, while low-risk group had more the GCB type DLBCL (Figure 5C).
evidence: This association between riskScore and DLBCL subtype is shown in Figure 5C based on GSE53786 dataset.

claim: High-risk group displayed higher lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) ratio.
source: Besides, high-risk group displayed higher lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) ratio (Figure 5F).
evidence: This association is shown in Figure 5F based on GSE53786 dataset.

claim: The riskScore was associated with poor prognosis (p<0.001, HR = 1.545, 95% CI 1.284–1.861) in univariate analysis.
source: As expected, the riskScore was associated with the poor prognosis (Figure 5G, p<0.001, HR = 1.545, 95% CI 1.284–1.861)
evidence: This univariate Cox regression result is shown in Figure 5G with statistical significance.

claim: The riskScore was an independent prognostic factor (p=0.002, HR = 1.474, 95% CI 1.156–1.879) in multivariate analysis.
source: and was an independent prognostic factor (Figure 5H, p=0.002, HR = 1.474, 95% CI 1.156–1.879).
evidence: This multivariate Cox regression result is shown in Figure 5H with statistical significance.

claim: Patients with high expression of VCAN had higher OS rate (p=0.003) in CHCAMS cohort.
source: The survival analysis showed that patients with high expression of VCAN had higher OS rate (Figure 6A, p=0.003).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Patients with high CD3G+ T cells infiltration showed favorable prognosis (p<0.001) in CHCAMS cohort.
source: The survival analysis revealed that patients with high CD3G+ T cells infiltration showed favorable prognosis (Figure 6B, p<0.001).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Patients in high C1QB expression group showed adverse prognosis (p=0.015) in CHCAMS cohort.
source: For C1QB, the patients in high expression group (cut-off=82.41) showed adverse prognosis (Figure 6C, p=0.015).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6C.

claim: CD68 + macrophages account for (17.75±1.05)% ratio in DLBCL.
source: As was shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, CD68 + macrophages [(17.75±1.05) %] account for more ratio than CD4 + T cells [(0.68±0.20) %] and CD8 + T cells [(6.69±0.56) %] (p<0.001, Kruskal-Wallis Test and Dunn's Test).
evidence: This quantification is based on IHC analysis of CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD4 + T cells account for (0.68±0.20)% ratio in DLBCL.
source: As was shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, CD68 + macrophages [(17.75±1.05) %] account for more ratio than CD4 + T cells [(0.68±0.20) %] and CD8 + T cells [(6.69±0.56) %] (p<0.001, Kruskal-Wallis Test and Dunn's Test).
evidence: This quantification is based on IHC analysis of CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD8 + T cells account for (6.69±0.56)% ratio in DLBCL.
source: As was shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, CD68 + macrophages [(17.75±1.05) %] account for more ratio than CD4 + T cells [(0.68±0.20) %] and CD8 + T cells [(6.69±0.56) %] (p<0.001, Kruskal-Wallis Test and Dunn's Test).
evidence: This quantification is based on IHC analysis of CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD68 + macrophages were associated with better prognosis (p=0.029) in CHCAMS cohort.
source: In the survival analysis of these three types of immune cells, we found that CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells were associated with better prognosis (Figure 6D–F, p=0.029, p=0.002, p=0.053).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6D.

claim: CD8 + T cells were associated with better prognosis (p=0.002) in CHCAMS cohort.
source: In the survival analysis of these three types of immune cells, we found that CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells were associated with better prognosis (Figure 6D–F, p=0.029, p=0.002, p=0.053).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6E.

claim: CD4 + T cells were associated with better prognosis (p=0.053) in CHCAMS cohort.
source: In the survival analysis of these three types of immune cells, we found that CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells were associated with better prognosis (Figure 6D–F, p=0.029, p=0.002, p=0.053).
evidence: This survival analysis result is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The ratio of CD3G+ T cells was positively correlated with that of CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells.
source: Besides, the ratio of CD3G+ T cells was positively correlated with that of CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells, C1QB expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells, and VCAN expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells ratio (Figure 6G).
evidence: This correlation analysis is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6G.

claim: C1QB expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells.
source: Besides, the ratio of CD3G+ T cells was positively correlated with that of CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells, C1QB expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells, and VCAN expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells ratio (Figure 6G).
evidence: This correlation analysis is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6G.

claim: VCAN expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells ratio.
source: Besides, the ratio of CD3G+ T cells was positively correlated with that of CD68 + macrophages, CD8 + T cells, and CD4 + T cells, C1QB expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells, and VCAN expression level was positively correlated with CD8 + T cells ratio (Figure 6G).
evidence: This correlation analysis is based on IHC data from CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6G.

claim: M1 macrophages accounted for more proportion than M2 macrophages in GSE53786 and GSE32918 datasets.
source: And XCELL and QUANTISEQ algorithms revealed that M1 macrophages accounted for more proportion than M2 macrophages in GSE53786 and GSE32918 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1L–O), which was confirmed in the CHCAMS cohort (Figure 6—figure supplement 1P).
evidence: This finding is based on computational analysis using XCELL and QUANTISEQ algorithms on GEO datasets, shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1L–O.

claim: CD3G+ T cells ratio was higher in DLBCL originated from groin and testis.
source: It turned out that CD3G+ T cells ratio was higher in DLBCL originated from groin and testis, and VCAN featured higher expression in lymph node-originated DLBCL (Figure 6J–K, p<0.05, p<0.01, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–K).
evidence: This association with tumor location is based on IHC analysis of CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6J.

claim: VCAN featured higher expression in lymph node-originated DLBCL.
source: It turned out that CD3G+ T cells ratio was higher in DLBCL originated from groin and testis, and VCAN featured higher expression in lymph node-originated DLBCL (Figure 6J–K, p<0.05, p<0.01, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–K).
evidence: This association with tumor location is based on IHC analysis of CHCAMS cohort shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Patients in high-risk group could be sensitive to Carmustine, Cytarabine, Oxaliplatin, Vincristine, Vorinostat, and Bortezomib in GSE53786 dataset.
source: As is shown in Figure 7A (prediction of GSE53786), patients in high-risk group could be sensitive to Carmustine, Cytarabine, Oxaliplatin, Vincristine, Vorinostat, and Bortezomib, but no drug could work better in low-risk group.
evidence: This drug sensitivity prediction is based on oncoPredict analysis of GSE53786 dataset shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In GSE32918, Carmustine, Cytarabine, Oxaliplatin, Vorinostat, Afuresertib, Bortezomib, Ibrutinib, and Tamoxifen could work better in high-risk group.
source: And in GSE32918 (Figure 7B), Carmustine, Cytarabine, Oxaliplatin, Vorinostat, Afuresertib, Bortezomib, Ibrutinib, and Tamoxifen could work better in high-risk group, and Vincristine (sensitivity score: low-risk vs high-risk=0.219±0.026 vs 0.223±0.031) could work better in low-risk group.
evidence: This drug sensitivity prediction is based on oncoPredict analysis of GSE32918 dataset shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Carmustine, Cytarabine, Oxaliplatin, Vorinostat, and Bortezomib could be reliable candidates for treating high-risk patients based on the three TPGs signature prognostic model.
source: However, the intersection analysis of the drugs to which the high-risk patients in both datasets could be sensitive revealed that Carmustine, Cytarabine, Oxaliplatin, Vorinostat, and Bortezomib could be reliable candidates for treating high-risk patients based on the three TPGs signature prognostic model (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This conclusion is based on intersection analysis of drug sensitivity predictions from both GSE53786 and GSE32918 datasets.

claim: VCAN is also known as versican and is a crucial component of extracellular matrix.
source: VCAN, also known as versican, is a crucial component of extracellular matrix (Wight, 2017), and exists in several isoforms (Fujii et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement about VCAN is supported by citations to Wight, 2017 and Fujii et al., 2015.

claim: VCAN exists in several isoforms.
source: VCAN, also known as versican, is a crucial component of extracellular matrix (Wight, 2017), and exists in several isoforms (Fujii et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement about VCAN isoforms is supported by citation to Fujii et al., 2015.

claim: When VCAN is expressed by myeloid cells, it induces an anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive microenvironment.
source: When expressed by myeloid cells, VCAN induces an anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive microenvironment. Conversely, its expression by stromal cells typically leads to a pro-inflammatory response (Wight et al., 2020).
evidence: This functional role of VCAN is supported by citation to Wight et al., 2020.

claim: When VCAN is expressed by stromal cells, it typically leads to a pro-inflammatory response.
source: When expressed by myeloid cells, VCAN induces an anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive microenvironment. Conversely, its expression by stromal cells typically leads to a pro-inflammatory response (Wight et al., 2020).
evidence: This functional role of VCAN is supported by citation to Wight et al., 2020.

claim: In gastric cancer, high expression of VCAN has been associated with increased infiltration of fibroblasts, significant enrichment of stromal-associated signaling pathways, and poor prognosis.
source: In gastric cancer, high expression of VCAN has been associated with increased infiltration of fibroblasts, significant enrichment of stromal-associated signaling pathways, and poor prognosis (Song et al., 2022).
evidence: This association in gastric cancer is supported by citation to Song et al., 2022.

claim: In hepatocellular carcinoma, VCAN exhibits a strong association with immune checkpoint gene expression.
source: In hepatocellular carcinoma, VCAN exhibits a strong association with immune checkpoint gene expression (Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This association in hepatocellular carcinoma is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2022.

claim: Overexpression of VCAN V1 has an inhibitory effect on cell proliferation, partly due to its promotion of activation-induced cell death in lymphoid cell lines.
source: A study has shown that overexpression of VCAN V1 has an inhibitory effect on cell proliferation, partly due to its promotion of activation-induced cell death in lymphoid cell lines (Fujii et al., 2015).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citation to Fujii et al., 2015.

claim: C1q is synthesized in the tumor microenvironment and functions as an extracellular matrix protein.
source: C1q is synthesized in the tumor microenvironment and functions as an extracellular matrix protein, and C1QB is a component of C1q (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement about C1q is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2022.

claim: C1QB is a component of C1q.
source: C1q is synthesized in the tumor microenvironment and functions as an extracellular matrix protein, and C1QB is a component of C1q (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement about C1QB is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2022.

claim: High C1q expression in TME is associated with a poor prognosis in non-small cell lung carcinoma and gastric cancer.
source: However, the majority of these results, as observed in non-small cell lung carcinoma and gastric cancer, indicate that high C1q expression in TME is associated with a poor prognosis (Li et al., 2023; Mangogna et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2020).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citations to Li et al., 2023; Mangogna et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2020.

claim: C1QB has been found to exert an impact on the TME and is positively associated with infiltration levels of CD8 + T cell, as well as with M1 and M2 macrophages in osteosarcoma.
source: Additionally, C1QB has been found to exert an impact on the TME and is positively associated with infiltration levels of CD8 + T cell, as well as with M1 and M2 macrophages in osteosarcoma (Chen et al., 2021a).
evidence: This association in osteosarcoma is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021a.

claim: C1QB expression shows a positive correlation with predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy, such as PD-L1 expression and CD8 + T cell infiltration.
source: Moreover, C1QB expression shows a positive correlation with predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy, such as PD-L1 expression and CD8 + T cell infiltration (Jiang et al., 2020).
evidence: This correlation is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2020.

claim: In malignant melanoma, C1QB promotes proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inhibiting cell apoptosis.
source: Furthermore, in malignant melanoma, C1QB promotes proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inhibiting cell apoptosis (Zheng et al., 2021), and the high-expression group exhibits significant enrichment of genes related to immune and apoptosis (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This functional role in melanoma is supported by citations to Zheng et al., 2021 and Yang et al., 2022.

claim: CD3G is a member of the TCR/CD3 complex primarily expressed in lymphocytes subgroups.
source: CD3G is a member of the TCR/CD3 complex primarily expressed in lymphocytes subgroups. It plays a crucial role in initiating the activation of T cells (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement about CD3G is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2008.

claim: CD3G plays a crucial role in initiating the activation of T cells.
source: CD3G is a member of the TCR/CD3 complex primarily expressed in lymphocytes subgroups. It plays a crucial role in initiating the activation of T cells (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This functional role is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2008.

claim: CD3G is involved in coupling antigen recognition.
source: It is also involved in coupling antigen recognition (Chen et al., 2021b).
evidence: This functional role is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021b.

claim: CD3G is reported to be associated with long-term OS and good prognosis in breast invasive carcinoma.
source: It is reported to be associated with long-term OS and good prognosis in breast invasive carcinoma (Wang et al., 2019) as well as in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2019.

claim: CD3G is reported to be associated with long-term OS and good prognosis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
source: It is reported to be associated with long-term OS and good prognosis in breast invasive carcinoma (Wang et al., 2019) as well as in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Macrophages can be roughly classified into two types based on their functional features: M1 or M2.
source: Macrophages can be roughly classified into two types based on their functional features: M1 or M2. M1 macrophages exert anti-tumor effects, whereas M2 macrophages promote tumor growth and progression in TME (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This classification is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: M1 macrophages exert anti-tumor effects.
source: Macrophages can be roughly classified into two types based on their functional features: M1 or M2. M1 macrophages exert anti-tumor effects, whereas M2 macrophages promote tumor growth and progression in TME (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This functional role is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: M2 macrophages promote tumor growth and progression in TME.
source: Macrophages can be roughly classified into two types based on their functional features: M1 or M2. M1 macrophages exert anti-tumor effects, whereas M2 macrophages promote tumor growth and progression in TME (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This functional role is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: Low infiltration of CD68 + macrophages was associated with an inferior prognosis in a previous study.
source: A previous study found that low infiltration of CD68 + macrophages was associated with an inferior prognosis (Croci et al., 2021).
evidence: This prognostic association is supported by citation to Croci et al., 2021.

claim: CD8 + T cells in DLBCL exhibit elevated levels of inhibitory molecules on their surface, such as PD-1, PD-L1, and TIM3.
source: However, in DLBCL, CD8 + T cells exhibits elevated levels of inhibitory molecules on their surface, such as PD-1, PD-L1, and TIM3.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of CD8+ T cells in DLBCL.

claim: High expression of TIM3 on CD8 + T cells has been associated with tumor progression and poor outcomes in DLBCL.
source: High expression of TIM3, an inhibitory immune checkpoint receptor, on CD8 + T cells has been associated with tumor progression and poor outcomes (Roussel et al., 2021; Xu-Monette et al., 2019).
evidence: This association is supported by citations to Roussel et al., 2021 and Xu-Monette et al., 2019.

claim: VCAN has the potential to modulate immune infiltration by reducing the immunosuppressive phenotype of immune cells.
source: VCAN has the potential to modulate immune infiltration by reducing the immunosuppressive phenotype of immune cells (Huang et al., 2021), thus enabling a more efficient anti-tumor response.
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2021.

claim: The high expression of VCAN might create a suppressive environment for PD-1 + CD8+ T cells.
source: Here, we propose a hypothesis that in our study, the observed high expression of VCAN might create a suppressive environment for PD-1 + CD8+ T cells (Wight et al., 2020; Hirani et al., 2021).
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis supported by citations to Wight et al., 2020 and Hirani et al., 2021.

claim: 190 patients from the Cancer Hospital Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences were enrolled in this study.
source: 190 patients from the Cancer Hospital Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, the CHCAMS cohort, were enrolled in this study (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the study cohort used for validation.

claim: All patients in the CHCAMS cohort received surgery or biopsy during September, 2010 and September, 2020.
source: All patients received surgery or biopsy during September, 2010 and September, 2020, and then standard follow-ups were carried out until March, 2023.
evidence: This describes the timeframe for patient enrollment and follow-up.

claim: The ESTIMATE algorithm was used to assess tumor purity.
source: Tumor purity was assessed by ESTIMATE (Estimation of Stromal and Immune cells in Malignant Tumor tissues using Expression data) algorithm (Yoshihara et al., 2013)
evidence: This describes the computational method used, supported by citation to Yoshihara et al., 2013.

claim: Genes with |r|≥0.5 and p-value <0.05 were defined as tumor purity-related genes (TPGs).
source: The genes with | r |≥0.5 and p-value <0.05 was defined as the TPGs (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the threshold criteria used to define TPGs in the study methodology.

claim: CD3G could be regarded as a marker of T cells.
source: For CD3G, previous study revealed that it was a component of T cell receptor complex, for which it could be regarded as a marker of T cells (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This interpretation is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2008.

claim: CD68 is a surface marker specific to macrophages.
source: Macrophages play a crucial role in TME, and CD68 is a surface marker specific to macrophages.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CD68.

claim: CD8 is widely recognized as a marker of CD8 + T cells, also known as cytotoxic T cells.
source: CD8 is widely recognized as a marker of CD8 + T cells, also known as cytotoxic T cells (Farhood et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Farhood et al., 2019.

claim: The study used datasets GSE53786 and GSE32918 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database.
source: The RNA-Sequence and clinical data of GSE53786 and GSE32918 datasets were downloaded from GEO database.
evidence: This describes the data sources used in the study.

claim: Drug sensitivity prediction was conducted utilizing 'oncoPredict' packages in R 4.1.3.
source: Drug sensitivity prediction was conducted utilizing 'oncoPredict' packages in R 4.1.3.
evidence: This describes the computational tool used for drug sensitivity analysis.
